metadata.title: Chronodynamic Relativity: Unifying Cosmic Expansion, Galactic Dynamics, Gravitational Lensing, and CMB Acoustic Peaks from a Single Environmental Scalar Field
metadata.description: Standard Lambda-CDM cosmology requires two dark sector components in non-baryonic cold dark matter (Omega_c approx 0.26) and dark energy (Omega_Lambda approx 0.69) to reconcile general relativity with astronomical observations. We present Chronodynamic Relativity, a covariant metric-scalar framework where both dark sector phenomena arise from a single scalar field rho_s(x,t) representing physical space density. Under linear cosmic expansion (a(t) = t/t_0), time dilation scales as eta(z) = (1+z)^(-n/2) with geometric exponent n = 4. Distance modulus predictions match 1,701 Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae across z = 0.001 to 2.26 with delta mu_RMS = 0.138 mag, achieving chi^2/dof = 0.985 with zero free cosmological parameters. On galactic scales, metric clock gradients introduce a non-linear algebraic root gravity law g_eff = 0.5 * [g_N + sqrt(g_N^2 + 4 * g_N * a_c)] governed by a dynamic acceleration invariant a_c(t) = (c / 4 pi) * H(t) = 1.635e-10 m/s^2. Across 175 SPARC galaxies (3,391 data points), the theory reproduces the empirical Radial Acceleration Relation with RMS residual 0.098 dex and reduced chi^2 = 1.04. Strong gravitational lensing is recovered via an exact factor-of-two optical metric deflection, predicting the Einstein radius of the Bullet Cluster 1E 0657-56 (theta_E = 31.4 arcsec) and El Gordo ACT-CL J0102-4915 (theta_E = 38.6 arcsec) within 4% of empirical lensing reconstructions. The primordial CMB acoustic peak scale evaluates from first principles to l_A = 301.4, matching Planck 2018 (l_A = 301.47 +/- 0.09). We demonstrate that Chronodynamic Relativity simultaneously accounts for cosmic expansion, galactic rotation curves, cluster gravitational lensing, and CMB acoustics without non-baryonic dark matter or dark energy.
